tasks.short: Receive payment or obtain credit authorization.

steps.what: Read the credit status for this customer.
inputs: this customer
account card when the counter colleague has written one
outputs: the account, the credit limit, and whether the account is open

inputs: the account, the credit limit, and whether the account is open
the amount the customer owes

steps.what: Obtain credit authorization and record the decision.
inputs: the account, the credit limit, and whether the account is open
what the customer asked to put on account
outputs: the credit decision the salesperson recorded

tasks.design: A paper account card at the counter lists the customer, the account, the credit limit, and whether the account is open. The salesperson reads it, then still takes the payment and still decides and writes whether credit is given. A missing row is the paper account note, read in the same lookup.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account status sat in a till note or in memory, so each sale on account started with a search.
tasks.enabler_now: Four fields on a handwritten card are enough. The card is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
tasks.still_hard: Taking the money, and deciding whether this customer may buy on credit, stay with the salesperson.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether this customer may buy on credit, and taking the payment.
tasks.altitude: Finding the account is shorter when the card is current. The salesperson still receives the payment and still records the credit decision.

reach.task: Keep the account card the salesperson reads before payment
reach.learn: To write the customer, the account, the credit limit, and whether the account is open, and to drop a row that is no longer true

evidence.claim: Taking payment and deciding credit are counter work. A card shortens finding the account. It does not take the money or decide the credit. Model knowledge.

A decision with significant effect may not be left solely to automation under the cited article. Whether this customer may buy on credit is decided by the salesperson and written by hand. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited article.

Tools fit to monitor staff, such as till cameras and per-cashier variance reports, need works-council consent, as does a system that processes staff data. This task adds no till camera, no per-cashier variance report, and no staff-performance log. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited statute.

assumptions: The boundary is one sale at the parts counter. Receiving payment and obtaining credit authorization keep their full time.

Account card fields are customer, account, credit limit, and whether the account is open. The producer is the counter colleague, when an account is opened or the limit changes. If a row is missing or stale, the salesperson reads the paper account note inside the lookup.
Screen time at the till stays inside the payment step. The card only shortens the search for the account. The credit decision is the salesperson's, written in s3.

The card is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code. Card upkeep is the counter colleague's 1.0 hours per 100 salesperson hours on this task. The salesperson's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether this counter has a colleague who writes the card, or the salesperson copies the account note.
How often the credit limit changes between sales.
research_questions: Of the account sales in a week, how many customers are already on the card, and how many credit decisions differ from the limit written there?

incremental.description: The salesperson adds no recurring chore. Taking payment and recording the credit decision stay in the steps above.
The counter colleague writes the account card by hand when an account is opened or the limit changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the account card has no row, the salesperson reads the paper account note inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Receiving payment and obtaining credit authorization never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer complaints and update customers on ordered parts.

steps.what: Read the back-order note for the parts this customer ordered.
inputs: this customer
back-order note when the stores colleague has written one
outputs: the part, the date promised, and whether it has arrived

steps.what: Assist customers by responding to customer complaints and updating them about those parts.
inputs: the part, the date promised, and whether it has arrived
what the customer says is wrong
outputs: what the salesperson told the customer about the complaint and the parts

tasks.design: A paper back-order note lists the part, the customer, the date promised, and whether the part has arrived. The salesperson reads it, then still hears the complaint and still tells the customer where those parts stand. A missing row is the delivery note, read in the same lookup.
tasks.previous_blocker: Whether a part had arrived lived on the delivery note in the stores room, so the counter hunted before answering.
tasks.enabler_now: The stores colleague writes four fields by hand when a delivery is booked or the part arrives. The note is paper.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing the complaint and telling the customer what is true stay a conversation at the counter.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what the customer is unhappy about and saying what is true about the parts.
tasks.altitude: Finding the back-order note is shorter when it is current. The salesperson still assists the customer and still gives the update in person.

reach.task: Keep the back-order note the salesperson reads before the update
reach.learn: To write the part, the customer, the date promised, and whether it has arrived, and to change the row when the delivery comes in

evidence.claim: Responding to a complaint and telling the customer about a part are counter conversation. A note shortens finding the promise and the arrival. It does not hear the complaint or speak to the customer. Model knowledge.
Emotion recognition at work is banned under the cited article. This conversation adds none. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited article.

assumptions: The boundary is one customer at the counter. Responding to the complaint and updating the customer keep their full time.

Back-order note fields are part, customer, date promised, and whether it has arrived. The producer is the stores colleague, when the delivery is booked or the part arrives. If a row is missing or stale, the salesperson reads the delivery note inside the lookup.
The complaint is heard in the conversation. It is not stored as a prepared reply. The note is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
Note upkeep is the stores colleague's 1.5 hours per 100 salesperson hours on this task. The salesperson's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: How often the promised date is wrong by the time the customer asks.
Whether complaints are mostly about late parts or about the wrong part.
research_questions: Of the complaint conversations in a week, how many parts already have a current row, and how many updates change after the customer speaks?

incremental.description: The salesperson adds no recurring chore. The complaint and the update stay in the conversation above.
The stores colleague writes the back-order note by hand when a delivery is booked or the part arrives.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the back-order note has no row, the salesperson reads the delivery note inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Responding to complaints and updating the customer never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Fill customer orders from stock or place orders.

steps.what: Read which bin holds the requested items.
inputs: the requested items
shelf card when the stores colleague has written one
outputs: the part, the bin, and whether it is on the shelf

steps.what: Fill the customer orders from the stock on that shelf.
inputs: the part, the bin, and whether it is on the shelf
the customer orders
outputs: the parts picked from the shelf for those customer orders

steps.what: Place orders for the requested items that are out of stock.
inputs: the requested items that were not on the shelf
the supplier the store uses for that part
outputs: the supplier order the salesperson placed

tasks.design: A paper shelf card lists the part, the bin, and whether it is on the shelf. The salesperson reads it, then still picks the parts off the shelf, and still places the order with the supplier when the shelf is empty. A missing row is a walk along the shelf, done in the same lookup.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bin locations lived on labels the salesperson had to walk to before every pick.
tasks.enabler_now: The stores colleague writes the part and the bin by hand when stock is put away. The card is paper.
tasks.still_hard: Picking the parts, noticing an empty shelf, and placing the order with the supplier stay manual.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing the shelf is empty and choosing what to ask the supplier for.
tasks.altitude: Finding the bin is shorter when the card is current. The salesperson still fills the order from stock and still places the supplier order.

reach.task: Keep the shelf card the salesperson reads before the pick
reach.learn: To write the part, the bin, and whether it is on the shelf, and to change the row when stock is put away or sold out

evidence.claim: Picking parts from a shelf and placing an order with a supplier are counter work. A card shortens finding the bin. It does not pick the parts or place the order. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one customer order at the parts counter. Filling from stock and placing the supplier order keep their full time.

Shelf card fields are part, bin, and whether it is on the shelf. The producer is the stores colleague, when stock is put away or the bin sells out. If a row is missing or stale, the salesperson walks the shelf inside the lookup.

An empty shelf is noticed by the salesperson during the pick. The supplier order is the salesperson speaking to the supplier. The card is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.

Card upkeep is the stores colleague's 1.5 hours per 100 salesperson hours on this task. The salesperson's own upkeep is zero. The same shelf card is read again on telephone orders, and that task does not count the upkeep a second time.
unknowns: How often the bin on the card is wrong because stock was moved.
How many requested items are out of stock on a typical day.
research_questions: Of the customer orders in a week, how many bins are current on the card, and how many items are out of stock after the pick?

incremental.description: The salesperson adds no recurring chore. Picking the parts and placing the supplier order stay in the steps above.
The stores colleague writes the shelf card by hand when stock is put away or the bin sells out.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the shelf card has no row, the salesperson walks the shelf inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Filling the customer orders and placing the supplier order never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive and fill telephone orders for parts.

steps.what: Read the parts named on these telephone orders.
inputs: the parts the caller named
shelf card when the stores colleague has written one
outputs: the part and the bin for these telephone orders

steps.what: Receive the telephone orders and fill them for the customer.
inputs: the part and the bin for these telephone orders
what the caller asks for
outputs: the telephone order the salesperson took and the parts filled for that caller

tasks.design: The same paper shelf card lists the part and the bin. The salesperson reads it during the call, then still takes the telephone order and still fills those parts for the caller. A missing row is the shelf label, read in the same lookup.
tasks.previous_blocker: Part and bin lived on the shelf, so a telephone order meant leaving the phone or guessing the bin.
tasks.enabler_now: The shelf card is already kept for the stock task. This task only reads it. The card is paper.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing the caller and filling the telephone order stay the salesperson's work on the phone.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing the part the caller wants and confirming what will be filled.
tasks.altitude: Finding the bin during the call is shorter when the card is current. The salesperson still receives the telephone order and still fills it.

reach.task: Keep the shelf card already used before a pick from stock
reach.learn: The part and the bin are written when stock is put away, which is counted on the stock task, not again here

evidence.claim: Taking a telephone order and filling the parts for the caller are counter work. A card shortens finding the bin while the caller waits. It does not take the call or pick the parts. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one telephone order. Receiving the call and filling the parts keep their full time. The call stays with the salesperson.
The parts card is the shelf card: part and bin. The producer is the stores colleague, when stock is put away. If a row is missing or stale, the salesperson reads the shelf label inside the lookup.

Shelf-card upkeep is counted on the stock-fill task, not again here. The salesperson's own upkeep on this task is zero. The card is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
unknowns: How often the caller names a part that is not on the shelf card.
How long the caller will wait while the salesperson checks a missing row.
research_questions: Of the telephone orders in a week, how many parts are already on the shelf card, and how many calls wait while the salesperson checks the shelf?

incremental.description: The salesperson adds no recurring chore. Taking the telephone order and filling the parts stay in the steps above. Shelf-card upkeep is counted on the stock-fill task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the shelf card has no row, the salesperson reads the shelf label inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Receiving the telephone order and filling it never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The salesperson still takes payment, decides credit, answers the complaint, updates the customer, picks the parts, places the order, and takes the telephone order. A card only shortens finding the account, the back-order note, or the bin.
reach: The counter colleague writes the customer, the account, the credit limit, and whether the account is open before payment is taken.
The stores colleague writes the part, the customer, the date promised, and whether it has arrived before the customer is updated.
The stores colleague writes the part and the bin before the pick from stock. Telephone orders read that same card.
skills_to_grow: Open the paper account note, the delivery note, or the shelf when the card has no row.
Decide credit from the customer in front of you, not from the card alone.
Do not let the card answer the complaint, pick the parts, or place the order.
role.ambitious_version: Cards do not take payment, authorize credit, answer complaints, update customers, pick parts, place orders, or take telephone orders. The salesperson still does.
